auto getMidpoint = [&](idx_t i1, idx_t i2) -> idx_t {\n                auto key = std::make_pair(std::min(i1, i2), std::max(i1, i2));\n                auto it = midpointCache.find(key);\n static_cast<idx_t>(vertices.size());\n                vertices.push_back(mid);\n                midpointCache[key] = idx;\n                return idx;\n            };\n\n            for (const auto& face : faces) {\n                idx_t a = getMidpoint(face[0], face[1]);\n                idx_t b = getMidpoint(face[1], face[2]);\n                idx_t c = getMidpoint(face[2], face[0]);\n\n c});\n            }\n            faces = std::move(newFaces);\n        }\n\n        // Build triangles (normals pointing inward for a \"room\")\n        triangles.reserve(faces.size());\n        for ============================================================================\n\nclass RandomGenerator {\n    std::mt19937 rng;\n    std::uniform_real_distribution<val_t> dist;\npublic:\n    explicit RandomGenerator(uint32_t seed = 42) : rng(seed), dist(0.0f, 1.0f) {}\n    val_t rand() { return dist(rng); }\n};\n\n// Generate a random point inside a triangle using barycentric coordinates\nVec3 randomPointInTriangle(const Triangle& t, RandomGenerator& rng) {\n    val_t u = rng.rand();\n    val_t v = rng.rand();\n    if (u + v > 1.0f) {\n        u = 1.0f - u;\n        v = 1.0f - v;\n    }\n arg-max scan.\n * Per-output summation order is preserved, so results match the sequential code.\n */\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <array>\n#include <cfloat>\n#include <chrono>\n#include y, val_t z) : x(x), y(y), z(z) {}\n    HD explicit constexpr Vec3(val_t v) : x(v), y(v), z(v) {}\n\n    HD Vec3 operator+(const Vec3& o) const { return {x + o.x, y + o.y, z + o.z}; }\n    HD Vec3 operator-(const Vec3& o) const { return {x - o.x, y - o.y, z - o.z}; }\n    HD Vec3 operator*(val_t s) const { return {x * s, y * s, z * s}; }\n    HD Vec3 operator/(val_t s) const { return {x / s, y   return {y * o.z - z * o.y, z * o.x - x * o.z, x * o.y - y * o.x};\n    }\n\n    HD val_t squaredNorm() const { return x * x + y * y + z * z; }\n    HD val_t norm() const { return sqrtf(squaredNorm()); }\n    HD Vec3 normalized() const {\n        val_t n = norm();\n        return n > EPSILON ? *this / n : Vec3();\n    }\n\n    HD bool operator==(const Vec3& o) const {\n        return fabsf(x - o.x) < EPSILON && fabsf(y - o.y) < EPSILON && fabsf(z - o.z) < EPSILON;\n    }\n};\n\n// Same semantics as std::min / std::max for arithmetic types (usable on device)\nHD inline val_t sMin(val_t a, val_t b) { return (b < a) ? b : a; }\nHD inline val_t sMax(val_t a, val_t b) { return (a < b) ? b : a; }\n\nstruct Triangle {\n    Vec3 a, b, c;\n    Vec3 _normal;\n\n    Triangle() = ============================================================================\n\n// Separating axis test for triangle-box overlap\nbool triangleBoxOverlap(const Vec3& boxCenter, const Vec3& boxHalfSize, const Triangle& tri) {\n    // Translate triangle to box center\n    Vec3 v0 = tri.a - boxCenter;\n    Vec3 v1 = tri.b - boxCenter;\n    Vec3 v2 = tri.c - boxCenter;\n\n    // Triangle edges\n    Vec3 e0 = v1 - v0;\n    Vec3 e1 = v2 - v1;\n    Vec3 e2 = v0 - v2;\n\n    // Test box normals (AABB axes)\n    auto minMax3 = [](val_t a, val_t b, val_t c) {\n        return std::make_pair(std::min({a, b, c}), std::max({a, b, c}));\n    };\n\n    auto [minX, maxX] = minMax3(v0.x, v1.x, v2.x);\n    if (minX > boxHalfSize.x || maxX < -boxHalfSize.x) return false;\n\n    auto [minY, maxY] = minMax3(v0.y, v1.y, v2.y);\n    if (minY > boxHalfSize.y || maxY < -boxHalfSize.y) return false;\n\n    auto [minZ, maxZ] = minMax3(v0.z, v1.z, v2.z);\n    if (minZ > boxHalfSize.z || maxZ < -boxHalfSize.z) return false;\n\n    // Test triangle normal\n    Vec3 triNormal = e0.cross(e1);\n    val_t d = triNormal.dot(v0);\n    val_t r = boxHalfSize.x * std::abs(triNormal.x) +\n              boxHalfSize.y * std::abs(triNormal.y) +\n              boxHalfSize.z * std::abs(triNormal.z);\n    if (std::abs(d) > r) return false;\n\n    // Test 9 edge cross products\n    auto testAxis = [&](const Vec3& axis) {\n        val_t p0 = axis.dot(v0);\n        val_t p1 = axis.dot(v1);\n        val_t p2 = axis.dot(v2);\n        val_t r = boxHalfSize.x * std::abs(axis.x) +\n                  boxHalfSize.y * std::abs(axis.y) +\n                  boxHalfSize.z * std::abs(axis.z);\n        auto [minP, maxP] = minMax3(p0, p1, p2);\n        return !(minP > r || maxP < -r);\n    };\n\n    Vec3 axes[3] = {{1,0,0}, {0,1,0}, {0,0,1}};\n    Vec3 edges[3] = {e0, e1, e2};\n    for (const auto& axis : axes) {\n        for (const auto& edge : edges) {\n            Vec3 crossAxis = axis.cross(edge);\n            if (crossAxis.squaredNorm() > EPSILON) {\n                if (!testAxis(crossAxis)) return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Octree for Spatial Acceleration (built on host, traversed on device)\n// ============================================================================\n\nconstexpr size_t MAX_OCTREE_TRIS = 8;\nconstexpr val_t MAX_OCTREE_LEAF_SIZE = 0.5f;\n\n// Flattened octree node used on the device.\n// A node is a leaf iff triCount > 0; leaves reference triIdx[triStart .. triStart+triCount).\nstruct DevNode {\n    Vec3 center;\n    Vec3 halfExtent;\n    int32_t child[8];\n    uint32_t triStart;\n    uint32_t triCount;\n};\n\nclass Octree {\npublic:\n    Vec3 minBound, maxBound;\n    Vec3 halfExtent, center;\n    std::unique_ptr<Octree> children[8];\n    std::vector<size_t> triangleIndices;  // Indices into the global triangle list\n    const std::vector<Triangle>* allTriangles;  // Pointer to all triangles\n\n    Octree() : allTriangles(nullptr) {}\n\n    void build(const std::vector<Triangle>& triangles) {\n        allTriangles = &triangles;\n        if (triangles.empty()) return;\n\n        // Compute bounding box\n        minBound = triangles[0].a;\n        maxBound = triangles[0].a;\n        for (const auto& tri : triangles) {\n            for (const auto* v : {&tri.a, &tri.b, &tri.c}) {\n                minBound.x = std::min(minBound.x, v->x);\n                minBound.y = std::min(minBound.y, v->y);\n                minBound.z = std::min(minBound.z, v->z);\n                maxBound.x = std::max(maxBound.x, v->x);\n                maxBound.y = std::max(maxBound.y, v->y);\n                maxBound.z = std::max(maxBound.z, v->z);\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Collect all indices\n        std::vector<size_t> allIndices(triangles.size());\n        for (size_t i = 0; i < triangles.size(); ++i) allIndices[i] = i;\n\n        buildNode(allIndices, minBound, maxBound);\n    }\n\nprivate:\n    void buildNode(const std::vector<size_t>& indices, const Vec3& nodeMin, const Vec3& nodeMax) {\n        minBound = nodeMin;\n        maxBound = nodeMax;\n        halfExtent = (maxBound - minBound) * 0.5f;\n        center = (minBound + maxBound) * 0.5f;\n\n        // If few enough triangles or too small, make this a leaf\n        if (indices.size() <= MAX_OCTREE_TRIS ||\n            (maxBound - minBound).norm() < MAX_OCTREE_LEAF_SIZE) {\n            triangleIndices = indices;\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // Subdivide into 8 children\n        Vec3 childHalfSize = halfExtent * 0.5f;\n        std::vector<size_t> childIndices[8];\n\n        for (size_t idx : indices) {\n            const Triangle& tri = (*allTriangles)[idx];\n\n            // Check which children this triangle overlaps\n            for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {\n                Vec3 childCenter = center;\n                childCenter.x += (i & 1) ? childHalfSize.x : -childHalfSize.x;\n                childCenter.y += (i & 2) ? childHalfSize.y : -childHalfSize.y;\n                childCenter.z += (i & 4) ? childHalfSize.z : -childHalfSize.z;\n\n                if (triangleBoxOverlap(childCenter,     break;\n            }\n        }\n\n        if (!canSplit) {\n            triangleIndices = indices;\n            return;\n        }\n\n        // Build children\n        for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {\n            if (!childIndices[i].empty()) {\n                Vec3 childMin = center;\n                Vec3 childMax = center;\n                childMin.x = (i & 1) ? center.x : minBound.x;\n children[i]->allTriangles = allTriangles;\n                children[i]->buildNode(childIndices[i], childMin, childMax);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n};\n\n// Append the subtree rooted at `node` }\n    nodes[id] = dn;\n    return id;\n}\n\n// ============================================================================\n// Mesh Generation: Icosphere\n// ============================================================================\n\n// Generate an icosphere by subdividing an icosahedron\nclass IcosphereMesh {\npublic:\n    std::vector<Triangle> triangles;\n\n    IcosphereMesh(int subdivisions, val_t radius) {\n        // Initial icosahedron vertices\n        const val_t t = (1.0f + std::sqrt(5.0f)) / 2.0f;\n\n        std::vector<Vec3> vertices = {\n            Vec3(-1,  t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 1,  t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3(-1, -t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 1, -t,  0).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 0, -1,  t).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 0,  1,  t).normalized() * radius,\n            Vec3( 0, -1, -t).normalized() * radius,\n        std::map<std::pair<idx_t, idx_t>, idx_t> midpointCache;\n\n            auto getMidpoint = [&](idx_t i1, idx_t i2) -> idx_t {\n                auto key = std::make_pair(std::min(i1, i2), = idx;\n                return idx;\n            };\n\n            for (const auto& face : faces) {\n                idx_t a = getMidpoint(face[0], face[1]);\n                idx_t b = getMidpoint(face[1], face[2]);\n                idx_t c = getMidpoint(face[2], face[0]);\n\n                newFaces.push_back({face[0], a, c});\n                newFaces.push_back({face[1], b, a});\n {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793114878125,"sessionID":"ses_e821cde84ffeeNyglJI396cwZI","part":{"id":"prt_17df97066001sTpRoHGT094gYH","messageID":"msg_17df968730016LK02f8ZWdKLQ8","sessionID":"ses_e821cde84ffeeNyglJI396cwZI","type":"reasoning","text":"The GPU kernel seems to be the real bottleneck at 69ms per chunk, totaling around 7s for 5120, while host RNG generation overlaps and stays hidden behind the synchronization wait of about 3.1s. I'm trying to reconcile why the total run time comes out to roughly 4.6s despite that.\n\nLooking closer, 101 chunks process 262k pairs times 16 rays each, giving about 61M ray-queries per second—pretty slow for a 3090 given each ray traverses an octree with dozens of triangle tests. The likely culprits are warp divergence from threads handling pairs with varying traversal depths, the dynamically-indexed stack array spilling into slow local memory, and the DevNode/Triangle struct reads hitting global memory with scattered access patterns rather than staying cached efficiently.\n\nPutting octree nodes in shared memory isn't feasible given the size at 20480 elements, though triangle data at around 1MB might fit in L2 cache reasonably well. I'm also wondering about occupancy limits from high register usage in the traversal kernel, and whether the real bottleneck is simply memory latency dominating over compute given how many box and triangle tests each ray requires.\n\nI'm now considering whether the N² × 16 rays × traversal cost is just inherent to the algorithm, and whether optimizations like read-only cache hints on pointers or better warp-level thread assignment could meaningfully reduce divergence and memory pressure.\n\nI'm also exploring a stackless traversal alternative using precomputed \"escape\" indices instead of an explicit stack — storing each node's first-child and next-subtree pointers so traversal can skip missed branches without recursion or local-memory overhead.\n\nIf the root is a leaf, its triangles get tested directly instead. For the stackless version, I'm storing nodes in DFS preorder with a skip index marking where the subtree ends, so each internal node's next pointer leads to its first child while a failed box test jumps straight to skip.\n\nThe skip pointers verify out as end-of-subtree indices, so each child's skip correctly leads to its next sibling, confirming traversal terminates properly at numNodes. This approach replaces the stack-based traversal with this linear skip scheme, doing roughly one box test per visited node instead of pre-checking all children before pushing.\n\nI'm also restructuring the node struct to drop the per-node child array and replace it with a single skip field, cutting memory to about 36 bytes per node, while keeping the box and triangle intersection math byte-for-byte identical to preserve correctness. Next I want to check occupancy and register usage for the kernel to make sure this layout change doesn't hurt performance.\n\nThe remaining logic around culling, ray-pair traversal, and early exits in computeKij all look fine as-is, so my focus now is checking ptxas output for register and local memory usage before implementing stackless traversal and re-measuring.\n\n","time":{"start":1793114861670,"end":1793114878056},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

Since all threads in a block share the same receiver row but diverge in traversal path per ray, that's probably causing warp divergence, while the node data itself should easily fit in cache for this problem size. I'm considering ways to boost parallelism, like restructuring how blocks and threads map to rows given the current 5120 blocks × 128 threads setup.\n\nRegister pressure looks like it caps occupancy around 50% rather than full utilization, which seems acceptable for now. {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793115013036,"sessionID":"ses_e821cde84ffeeNyglJI396cwZI","part":{"id":"prt_17dfb70700017S204G2Mw1n74D","messageID":"msg_17dfb699d001IjoH2NdLsEzkff","sessionID":"ses_e821cde84ffeeNyglJI396cwZI","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm puzzled that the kernel timing jumped from 69ms to 87ms per chunk—seems like stackless traversal might actually be slower here, possibly due to sequential dependent loads in the node-skip logic rather than any difference in box test counts.\n\nStepping back, I'm weighing bigger algorithmic restructuring options rather than micro-tuning: splitting each pair's rays across more threads for better latency hiding (at the cost of complexity in warp-level reduction), versus reorganizing memory access patterns for triangle data to reduce latency. The core bottleneck seems to be that each traversal visits ~40 nodes per ray with dependent pointer-chasing loads, making it fundamentally latency-bound.\n\nTrying to estimate throughput from first principles, I compute something like 7.6e9 pairs/s theoretical, but the observed rate is only ~3.7M pairs/s — roughly 300x slower than expected. That gap tells me something besides latency and divergence is dominating performance, possibly a memory-bound effect I haven't accounted for, so I need to reconsider what's actually limiting the kernel.\n\nI check the memory access patterns for draws, kij writes, and triangle reads — they all look reasonably coalesced, so that's not the bottleneck. That pushes me toward suspecting the octree traversal itself: a ray chord through the sphere interior likely intersects far more nodes than I assumed, maybe 50-100 leaves plus comparable internal nodes, each requiring box and triangle tests — which could easily explain the much higher actual cost per ray than my rough estimate.\n\nRecomputing with this higher visit count, I get roughly 40k flops per ray, scaling up to about 2 TFLOPS across all rays and pairs — which is actually plausible for the GPU given branchy, divergence-heavy code, putting us at maybe 5-10% of peak efficiency rather than something pathologically wrong. So the real lever isn't fixing a bug but reducing divergence and unnecessary work: triangle tests are unavoidable for hit leaves, and box tests can't be simplified without risking changing results due to epsilon tolerances, so the path forward is improving SIMT efficiency by getting threads in a warp to share work rather than diverge independently.\n\nDistributing rays within a pair across warp lanes (say 16 lanes per pair, 2 pairs per warp) might help somewhat, though per-ray divergence in traversal length still limits gains — realistically maybe 1.5-2x rather than a huge win. Looking at the bigger picture, the current implementation is already around 300x faster than the naive baseline, so further micro-optimization has diminishing returns; I'm also second-guessing whether switching to a stackless traversal actually made things slightly slower (69ms vs 87ms) or if that's measurement noise.\n\nThinking through why: the stack-based version tests all 8 children's boxes independently each step, giving good memory-level parallelism, while the stackless version's loads are chained dependently on the previous decision, making it latency-bound with worse MLP. That would explain the regression, suggesting I should consider reverting to the stack approach but store the stack in shared memory per thread instead — though a 32KB-per-block footprint for 128 threads would hurt occupancy, so I need to find a better balance.\n\nTrying other options: loading the whole octree and triangles into shared memory doesn't fit size-wise, and forcing non-coherent global loads via `__ldg` probably won't help much since sm_86 already caches reads in L1 by default. Warp-cooperative tracing doesn't apply here since each lane traces a different ray, so really the best path forward is to just benchmark the stack-based version directly rather than keep reasoning abstractly.\n\nThe measured numbers settle it: stack-based traversal averaged 69.2ms versus 86.8ms for stackless, and the 256-byte local stack (64 entries × 4 bytes) is small enough to stay L1-cached without real spill cost. So I'll revert to the stack-based traversal with the DevNode child[8] layout, then sweep block sizes (64/128/256) as a cheap follow-up optimization, and just trust that the algorithm already validated at smaller sizes holds for the 20480 run.\n\n","time":{"start":1793114992752,"end":1793115012931},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

 // prune this subtree\n            continue;\n        }\n        if (nd.triCount > 0) {\n            for (uint32_t k = 0; k < nd.triCount; ++k) {\n                const uint32_t idx = triIdx[nd.triStart + k];\n                if (idx == srcTriIdx || idx == dstTriIdx) continue;\n                const Triangle& tri = tris[idx];\n                val_t dist = rayTriangleIntersect(from, dirNorm, tri.a, tri.b, tri.c);\n                if (dist > EPSILON && dist < rayLen - EPSILON) return true;\n            }\n            n = nd.skip;\n        } else {\n            n = n + 1;  // descend into the first child\n        }\n    }\n    return false;","newString":"    // Depth-first traversal equivalent to Octree::applyToTris from the root.\n    // The root's own box is not tested;
